job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today, let's talk about sports safety. Rohan, if you twist your ankle, what is the first thing you do? Rohan: I use RICE, but I keep walking on it to prove I am tough. Teacher: That is dangerous! RICE helps, but it is not a cure-all. If you feel severe pain, you must stop playing immediately. Even if you can still walk, the injury could be serious. Priya: I thought a sprain was an injury to a muscle. Teacher: Actually, a sprain affects ligaments, while a strain affects muscles. Also, never apply heat to a fresh injury, as it increases swelling. Use ice instead. Rohan: What about concussions? If I don't faint, I am safe, right? Teacher: Not at all. A concussion is a brain injury that does not always cause fainting. Symptoms like dizziness or confusion might appear hours later, not just immediately. Priya: Should I stay in bed for days if I get hurt? Teacher: No, gentle movement is usually better than total bed rest once the initial pain settles. And remember, never wrap a bandage too tightly, as it cuts off circulation. Always listen to your body instead of trying to play through pain.

items.evidence: Also, never apply heat to a fresh injury, as it increases swelling.
items.q: Meena has just twisted her ankle and it is starting to swell. What should she put on it?
options: Ice, because heat would make the swelling worse
A hot pack, because heat brings the swelling down
A very tight bandage to squeeze the swelling out
Nothing at all, if she can still walk on it
items.explain: Heat increases swelling in a fresh injury, so the teacher says to use ice instead.

wrong.why: thinks heat reduces swelling in a fresh sprain
thinks a tighter bandage works better
thinks walking means the injury is not serious

items.evidence: Symptoms like dizziness or confusion might appear hours later, not just immediately.
items.q: Arjun bumps his head in a match and feels fine. Three hours later he feels dizzy. What does this show?
options: Concussion signs can show up hours after a hit
The dizziness came too late to be from the hit
He is safe from concussion because he never fainted
His head healed once the first pain went away
items.explain: Concussion symptoms like dizziness or confusion might appear hours later, not just right after the hit.

wrong.why: thinks concussion symptoms always appear immediately
thinks concussion happens only if you faint
thinks pain going away means healing

items.evidence: Actually, a sprain affects ligaments, while a strain affects muscles.
items.q: Priya hurt a ligament in her knee. Rohan hurt a muscle in his leg. What injuries do they have?
options: Priya has a sprain and Rohan has a strain
Priya has a strain and Rohan has a sprain
Both of them have a sprain
Both of them have a strain
items.explain: A sprain affects ligaments and a strain affects muscles, so Priya has a sprain and Rohan a strain.

wrong.why: thinks a strain is a ligament injury, swapping the two words
thinks a sprain is a muscle injury
thinks sprain and strain mean the same thing

items.evidence: Even if you can still walk, the injury could be serious.
items.q: Rohan twists his ankle badly during a game but can still walk on it. What should he do?
options: Stop playing, as the injury could still be serious
Keep playing, since walking shows it is not serious
Walk it off to show the team he is tough
Use RICE and keep playing, since RICE cures everything
items.explain: Being able to walk does not mean the injury is minor; it could still be serious, so he must stop.

wrong.why: thinks bearing weight means it cannot be serious
thinks playing through pain shows toughness
thinks RICE alone is enough for any injury
